Context: StarRocks-on-Sirius (GPU SQL engine embedded in a StarRocks compute node, "CN"). An SF1000 profiling campaign found four blockers; you are helping choose the best fix for one of them.
Read first: /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/sf1000-top4-fixes-plan.md (the plan: issues, candidate solutions, criteria, acceptance tests) and the relevant findings in /home/prestouser/.claude/plans/starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md (sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000 (WORKFLOW-PLAN.md indexes it; cn1-cnlog.txt, cn1-quent.txt, card-compare-*.txt, cn1/engine-cn0.log, cn1/dump/ are the raw material).
Source tree (read-only for you): /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf (engine C++ under src/, CN Rust under experimental/starrocks/src, translator under experimental/starrocks/crates/starrocks-plan-translator, StarRocks FE Java under experimental/starrocks/starrocks/fe, engine docs under docs/super-sirius/).
Rules: do not modify the source tree, do not start clusters or GPU jobs, write only under /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/. Distinguish measured facts from inference. Cite file:line for every mechanism you rely on.

Issue: Fail fast in the OOM reschedule loop. Three designs were written to /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/oom-failfast-surgical.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/oom-failfast-robust.md, /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/oom-failfast-upstream.md. Their structured summaries: [
 {
  "summary": "Fail fast at the reservation gate in gpu_pipeline_executor::manager_loop: inside the existing \"after downgrade, reservation still partial\" branch (gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:262-272), abort the query when the task is a retry, the downgrade freed 0 bytes, and reservation->size() + get_available_memory() is below the bytes its last OOM proved it needs (live_allocated + requested, a new size_t recorded beside the existing retry floor in gpu_pipeline_task.hpp). MAX_RETRIES=100 and the 50 ms backoff are untouched; the cross-GPU contention, CUDA-launch and sink-deferral retry paths never satisfy the predicate. Full design with code excerpts: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/oom-failfast-surgical.md",
  "mechanism": "Two facts the engine already certifies make the abort safe. (A) memory_space::make_reservation (cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-266) returns a partial grant only after notification_channel::wait() reports IDLE, which requires _n_active_notifiers == 0 (notification_channel.cpp:49-60); every reservation owns a notifier for its lifetime (reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:365-381, memory_reservation.hpp:183-198), so a partial grant means no in-flight reservation can free memory, and the grant is min(request, limit - allocated) (do_reserve_upto :535-543). (B) request_downgrade(...).get() returns bytes freed after sweeping TIER 1 repositories and TIER 2 queued tasks (downgrade_executor.cpp:223-300, :388-397); freed == 0 means nothing visible is convertible (parked sink output escapes the managers, streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112). (C) The OOM handlers already compute live_allocated + requested (gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:433-491 and :638-661) and fold it into update_retry_reservation_floor_after_oom (gpu_pipeline_task.hpp:99-108); the change records that sum as _oom_required_bytes, inherits it across reschedules (:110-114, executor :389), and the gate compares grant + available against it for retry_count > 0 && freed == 0. On a hit it logs, calls completion_handler->report_error(runtime_error(msg)) and breaks out of the manager loop exactly like the four existing gate failure paths (:195, :238, :260, :295); task_scheduler::drain_after_error restarts the loop (task_scheduler.cpp:265-311 -> task_executor.cpp:96-128). The message names bytes needed vs grantable, bytes held outside any live reservation vs pool, downgrade freed 0, retry number. It reaches the client unchanged through sirius_engine::execute (sirius_engine.cpp:263-278) -> streaming_fragment::run (:204-227) -> ffi::Fragment::run (sirius_ffi.cpp:990-1027) -> cxx::Exception (rust/crates/sirius/src/lib.rs:356) -> engine.rs:693-695 \"failed to execute fragment\" -> run_ready_fragment results.fail_query (compute_node_service.rs:864-910) -> fetch_data INTERNAL_ERROR (:523-528) -> FE ERROR 1064, the chain measured in cn1/runs/q05.r0.err. Measured basis: 17,917/17,917 gate passes in the six failure windows freed 0 and were partial (grant 3.08-3.32 GB vs floor up to 6.64 GB, q05), every OOM at global usage == 107374182400, no rescheduled task ever succeeded (retry_stats.py), 0 reschedule/partial lines outside the six windows on 1 CN and 0 on all cn4 CNs in the 4-CN window.",

   "SF1000 arm B: 15 passing queries x3; warm medians within noise of perf/sf1000/results.md cn1 column, compare.py MATCH set unchanged, 0 'cannot make progress' and 0 'reschedule (retry' lines in the engine log; optional arm C on 4 CNs"

  "predicted_effect": "Time-to-fail for the six drops from 54-232 s to about first-OOM + one retry round: q05 1.8-2.8 s (was 101.5), q08 1.9-4.3 (168.3), q09 2.6-4.9 (232.5), q17 1.4-2.6 (103.9), q18 9.5-10.2 (54.2; 9.3 s is its own senders parking 64.7 GB before the first OOM, so an absolute <= 5 s bar cannot be met and the criterion should be measured from the first OOM), q21 2.9-4.0 (114.5). Sum 774.9 s -> ~20-29 s; the 910 s 1-CN sweep -> ~160 s (82-83% shorter). Engine log shrinks ~87,000 lines per sweep (reschedule WARNs 17,900 -> <= 179); q05 GPU_SCAN Computing wasted on split re-reads 229.5 s -> ~2-3 s. Error text names needed vs grantable bytes and bytes held outside reservations vs the 100 GB pool. The 15 passing queries: predicate unreachable (0 partial-after-OOM lines in their windows on 1 and 4 CNs), no timing or result change. The six still fail on 1 CN (fixes 3/4) and the 0-38 GB post-failure leak remains (fix 2), though it now steals 0.4-6.4 s less engine time per failure.",

   "False positive if non-reservation memory is released externally between the OOM and the retry gate (unpin_table, a CN dropping another query's parked slot, a standalone QueryEnd with no HOST tier): bounded because today such a task only had 5-9 s of patience and fragments run one at a time per CN engine thread; optional two-line hysteresis (abort on the 2nd consecutive stalled retry) costs ~1 s if reviewers want it",

  "summary": "Progress-gated futility abort for the OOM reschedule loop. The reservation gate (gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:163-296) flags a retried task's attempt as futile only when four independent signals agree: the downgrade sweep that just ran freed 0 bytes, the granted reservation is below the task's OOM-derived retry floor, no task has completed anywhere on the context since this task was rescheduled, and no first-attempt task is in flight on any executor. The reschedule path (:311-419) counts an attempt as futile only if it was flagged AND then OOMed (and the epoch is still unchanged); after max_futile_attempts (default 2, configurable, 0 disables) consecutive futile attempts the query is failed with an error naming usage/limit, resident bytes outside live reservations, grant vs floor, bytes freed and attempts. MAX_RETRIES=100 and the 50 ms backoff stay as the hard cap/pacing (now sirius.executor.pipeline.oom_retry config), so the cross-GPU batch-lock contention case (prepare-path OOM with a full grant and a first attempt running on the other GPU) keeps today's budget. Full design with code excerpts and file:line at /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/oom-failfast-robust.md.",
  "mechanism": "New shared struct execution_progress {completed_epoch, inflight_first_attempts} owned by task_scheduler and passed to every gpu_pipeline_executor (GPU and HOST tiers, task_scheduler.cpp:117-124). Manager thread: after the existing downgrade branch (freed, reservation->size(), reservation_info.retry_reservation_floor all in scope, :225-273), for a retried task (cur_local->original_task_id set) compute gate_flagged_futile = (freed==0 && grant<floor && completed_epoch==local.progress_epoch_at_reschedule && inflight_first_attempts==0) || grant>=space_max; store on the local state, log DEBUG, still dispatch with the partial reservation (partials can succeed). Also: has_error() early-out before make_reservation so a post-error manager never blocks ~40 ms per queued retry; first attempts increment inflight_first_attempts before dispatch with an RAII decrement inside the lambda. Worker thread (catch task_reschedule_exception): if cur_local->gate_flagged_futile and the epoch is still unchanged, futile_attempts = prev+1 else 0; if futile_attempts >= policy.max_futile_attempts -> SIRIUS_LOG_ERROR + completion_handler->report_error(runtime_error(message)) and return (same exit shape as the exceeded-retries path :349-364; drain_after_error does the rest); else carry futile_attempts and a fresh epoch snapshot into the new local state alongside the retry floor (:389), sleep policy.backoff, reschedule. completed_epoch increments where _tasks_executed does today (:310). oom_reschedule_exception gains optional oom_details{requested_bytes, global_usage, peak_allocated_bytes} filled at the three throw sites (gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:489, :661, :748) for the message. Error text reaches the client verbatim through sirius_engine.cpp:268 -> engine.rs:291-316 -> compute_node_service.rs:864-905 -> result_store.rs fail_query -> FE getNext (cluster.log:6050-6054, runs/q05.r0.err). Config: exec::oom_retry_policy{max_retries=100, backoff=50ms, max_futile_attempts=2} inside a new gpu_pipeline_executor_config{thread_pool, oom_retry} mirroring downgrade_executor_config (exec/config.hpp:39-58), parsed from sirius.executor.pipeline with the old keys unchanged (sirius_config.cpp:139-144, :692). Contention case is excluded twice: the pool is not at its limit so the partial branch is never entered, and the batch holder is a first attempt in flight on the other executor. Behaviour on the 15 passing queries: oom_resched=0 for all and all 17,917 '0 bytes freed' lines fall inside the six failing windows, so the changed branch is never entered; cost is three uncontended atomics per task.",

  "summary": "Keep MAX_RETRIES=100 and the 50 ms backoff; add one new terminal condition next to the retry-cap check in gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp's reschedule path. An OOM retry is futile when the task is already a retry, the reservation gate for this attempt saw the downgrade free 0 bytes and could grant less than the OOM-derived retry floor, and no task completed on this executor since the retry was scheduled (_tasks_executed unchanged). The gate records a small retry_gate_observation on the task's local state; a pure, header-only predicate decides; the failure goes through the existing completion_handler->report_error path with a message naming bytes held outside any reservation vs the pool limit. Engine-only, no new config key, one Self-contained PR against dev. Full design with code excerpts and file:line citations: /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/fix/designs/oom-failfast-upstream.md",

# Plan: best solutions for the four SF1000 blockers, and the workflows that deliver them

Written 2026-09-03 15:20 UTC from the report `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-planning-cardinality-backpressure.md`
(sections 3B, 3C, 4). Evidence bundle: session scratchpad `perf/sf1000/` (indexed by `WORKFLOW-PLAN.md` there).
Working tree for all code: `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/fix-*` worktrees of the sirius-stacks clone,
one branch per fix off `perf/profile-sf1000` (45dab3be = d24f02c4 + aggregate gate + async dispatch + Quent probes).
Never the shared clone `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius`. No pushes, no PRs until asked.

## The four issues

| # | issue | where it lives | measured cost today (SF1000, 1 CN, 100 GiB pool) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | The OOM reschedule loop has no feasibility check | `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp` (:263 reservation gate, :330-420 reschedule, MAX_RETRIES=100, 50 ms sleep) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 take 54-232 s to die (775 s of a 910 s sweep); 17,917 "0 bytes freed, proceeding with partial reservation" lines |
| 2 | No per-query parked-output bookkeeping | `experimental/starrocks/src/engine.rs` (:291-316 process-wide wipe on Err), `compute_node_service.rs` (:449-476 cancel is result-store only), `local_exchange.rs` (removals only in take_ready) | 0-38 GB of a dead query's parked output survives into later queries; dead query's queued senders still run (q22 cold 4110 vs 943 ms) |
| 3 | The FE plans every FILES() scan at 1 row | StarRocks FE `StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode` (:664-676), `TableFunctionTable.java` (file sizes at :611, schema RPC), `PGetFileSchemaResult` (proto :647-650), CN `file_schema.rs` | every distribution decision is data-blind: 1 CN broadcasts 3.79B lineitem rows into q04's semi join, 4 CNs shuffle 3.23B rows for q03; all six failures are one plan shape |
| 4 | Six queries cannot run on 1 CN | fragment cut (FE) + receiver-first full materialisation (`engine.rs` run_fragment_inner, `local_exchange.rs`) + parked repositories outside the downgrade sweep (`src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, `src/downgrade/downgrade_executor.cpp:223-300`) | q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 OOM; standalone Sirius runs them in 2.7-6.5 s |

## Candidate solutions to weigh (input to the design workflow, not the decision)

1. **Fail fast.** (a) Abort at the reservation gate when `retry_count > 0 && freed == 0 && retry floor > grant`; (b) abort in the reschedule path when downgrade freed 0 and pool usage == limit and nothing completed since the previous attempt; (c) a bounded wall-clock/attempt budget per original task that scales with observed progress; (d) keep 100 retries for the batch-lock contention case (arrives via `rmm::out_of_memory` from `lock_or_prepare_batch`, not via the gate). Must produce an error that names parked bytes vs pool.
2. **Bookkeeping.** (a) `query_id` on every `ParkedOutput`, drop only the failing query's slots; (b) failed-query set on the engine thread that skips pending `Run`s; (c) `cancel_plan_fragment` drops the cancelled query's parked outputs and dequeues its fragments (needs a by-query removal in `LocalExchange`); (d) `drop_parked` in `run_ready_fragment`'s Err arm for pre-run translation failures; (e) a periodic sweep as a safety net. Order of landing matters: (a)+(d) are pure hygiene, (b)/(c) touch the dispatch contract.
3. **Cardinalities.** (a) FE-only: rows = total bytes / row width from the inferred schema in `computeFileScanNode`, using `TableFunctionTable` file sizes (no wire change; column stats stay UNKNOWN); (b) exact `num_rows` from parquet footers: new field in `PGetFileSchemaResult`, filled by the CN's `file_schema.rs` (proto + FE + CN); (c) later, per-column min/max from row-group stats; (d) no-FE alternative: CN-side translator refusal/hints, SQL join hints. Delivered as a patch in `experimental/starrocks/patches/` applied by `apply-starrocks-patches.sh`, so the FE must be rebuilt (`pixi run fe-build`). Predicted effect must be checked with `EXPLAIN COSTS` at 1 and 4 CNs: the source skeptic warns that `BROADCAST_JOIN_MEM_EXCEED_PENALTY` and zero single-node shuffle cost may still put lineitem across an exchange on 1 CN.
4. **Run the six on 1 CN.** (a) Same-node fragment fusion before translation: replace a receiver's `EXCHANGE_NODE` with its single local sender's node list at the `TPlan` level when every destination is this CN, so the fused plan is the standalone plan (needs `RIGHT_SEMI` in the translator for q21, finding P5); (b) spillable parked repositories: register streaming-sink outputs and receiver inputs with a registry the downgrade executor sweeps as a third tier, HOST-tier `output_row_count` and `export_packed` (five of six then fit in GPU+HOST = 279 GB; q09 marginal); (c) streaming receivers (build side first, probe streamed) is the long-term fix but touches the engine's single-flight lifecycle; (d) FE-side: real cardinalities (issue 3) may already move lineitem to the probe side of a broadcast join, which the engine can stream. The design must say which combination actually makes each of the six pass and what each costs.

## Evaluation criteria (judges score 1-5 each)

1. Does it fix the measured failure at SF1000 on this box (which queries, predicted numbers, how verified)?
2. Correctness risk and blast radius (which paths change for the 15 passing queries; determinism; cancellation).
3. Size and reviewability as an upstream PR (target layer in the carve plan: engine `src/` -> dev PR; CN `experimental/starrocks` -> fork PR; FE -> checked-in patch), tests it needs.
4. Effort and dependencies (what must land first; FE rebuild; proto change).
5. Measurability: an acceptance test that a reviewer can rerun in minutes plus the SF1000 arm.

## Acceptance tests (must exist before implementation is "done")

| fix | unit / component test | SF1000 verification (orchestrator-run, one arm at a time) |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Catch2 test in `test/cpp/pipeline/` driving a task through the reschedule path with a memory space that never frees: query fails within a bounded number of attempts with the new error text; contention case still retries | 1 CN, q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21: time-to-fail <= 5 s each (was 54-232 s), error names parked bytes; the 15 passing queries unchanged (warm medians within noise, `compare.py` set unchanged) |
| 2 | Rust tests in `engine.rs`/`local_exchange.rs`/`compute_node_service.rs`: failure drops only that query's slots; queued senders of a failed query are skipped; cancel drops parked outputs; translation failure drops slots in hand | 1 CN sweep in the same order as before: `[gpu_pool] allocated` returns to baseline after each failure (was +4.7..+38 GB), q22 cold no longer inflated, no `fragment run started` for a dead query after its failure |
| 3 | FE unit test (Java) for the new statistics path; CN test if the proto changes; `EXPLAIN COSTS` golden outputs for q03 q04 q05 q22 at 1 and 4 CNs showing real cardinalities and the new join sides | 1 CN and 4 CN sweeps of the 15 passing queries plus the six: plan shapes recorded, timings vs the campaign table, oracle compares |
| 4 | Fusion: translator/CN tests that a single-destination local exchange fuses and the fused plan matches the sender+receiver plan; spill: Catch2 test that a parked repository is swept to HOST and relayed back | 1 CN: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 pass with oracle MATCH; report their times against standalone (2.7-6.5 s) |

## Workflows

**A. Design exploration (`fix/design-workflow.js`).** Per issue, three independent designers with different angles (surgical minimum, robust design, what upstream would accept), each reads the report finding, the evidence and the code and returns a design (mechanism, files, tests, risks, predicted effect). Two judges per issue score the three against the criteria and pick or merge. One synthesizer per issue writes the spec `scratchpad/fix/designs/<issue>-SPEC.md`. A final integrator checks the four specs for interactions (fail-fast vs bookkeeping ordering; fusion vs spill vs cardinalities) and writes the build order.

**B. Implementation (`fix/implement-workflow.js`).** Per issue in its own worktree: implementer (tests first, then code, build, run the unit tests; commits with Conventional Commits and the Claude trailer), adversarial reviewer, fixer, verifier (fresh build + tests + clippy/fmt/pre-commit). Agents never start clusters or use GPUs other than the one assigned to their worktree (fix 1: GPU 0, fix 2: GPU 1, fix 3: none, fix 4: GPU 2). The orchestrator then runs the SF1000 arms from the table above, one at a time, and an integration branch with all four for the final sweep.

**C. Report.** `starrocks-sirius-perf/sf1000-top4-fixes-report.md`: per fix, what changed, tests, SF1000 before/after, what is left; plus the PR plan (branch, base, size) for when pushing is asked for.

## Status log
- 15:20 UTC: worktrees `fix-oom-failfast`, `fix-parked-bookkeeping`, `fix-files-cardinality`, `fix-fragment-fusion` being created and built; design workflow launched.

# Fix 1 design (upstream-acceptable angle): fail an OOM retry chain that cannot make progress

Written 2026-09-03 from the worktree `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` at `45dab3be`
(engine source cited as `src/...`, cucascade as `cucascade/...`) and the evidence bundle
`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/` (cited as `E/...`). Every number below is **measured** from a named file
unless marked **inference**.

## 0. One-paragraph summary

Keep `MAX_RETRIES = 100` and the 50 ms backoff exactly as they are. Add one new terminal condition
next to the existing retry-cap check in the executor's reschedule path: an OOM retry is **futile**
when (1) the task is already a retry, (2) at this attempt's reservation gate the downgrade freed
0 bytes and the space could grant less than the floor the previous OOM established, and (3) no task
has completed on this executor since the retry was scheduled. The gate records what it saw on the
task's local state (three integers); the reschedule path applies a pure predicate and fails the
query through the same `completion_handler->report_error` path the retry cap uses, with a message
that names the bytes held outside any reservation vs the pool limit. Engine-only (`src/`), no new
configuration key, one Self-contained PR against `dev`, tested by a GPU-free Catch2 predicate test
plus two new cases in the existing `test_oom_reschedule.cpp`. Predicted SF1000 effect: the six
failing queries die 2-5 s after their first OOM instead of 52-230 s later; the 15 passing queries
never enter the changed code path (0 partial-reservation lines in their windows on cn1 and cn4).

## 1. The measured failure (what the code must recognise)

**The loop.** `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:348-349` `static constexpr uint32_t
MAX_RETRIES = 100; if (next_retry_count > MAX_RETRIES) {...report_error...}`; `:409`
`std::this_thread::sleep_for(std::chrono::milliseconds(50));`; the only other exit is
`:312-316` (completion handler already in error). Each retry re-enters `manager_loop()` and the
reservation gate (`:143-296`).

**The gate proceeds on a partial grant.** `:196-272`: when `reservation->size() < bytes_needs`
the executor releases the partial reservation, calls `_downgrade_executor->request_downgrade(...)`
(`:224-233`, returns `size_t freed`), re-reserves, and if still short logs
```
:263  SIRIUS_LOG_WARN("GPU Pipeline Executor: after downgrade ({} bytes freed), reservation "
:265                  "still partial ({}/{} bytes) for pipeline {} task {} -- proceeding "
:266                  "with partial reservation", ...)
```
and dispatches anyway (`:284-301`). `freed`, `reservation->size()`, `bytes_needs`, and
`reservation_info.retry_reservation_floor` are all locals at that point.

**Why the grant is partial and why it never changes.** `cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-267`
```
std::unique_ptr<reservation> memory_space::make_reservation(size_t size)
{
  std::unique_ptr<reservation> res = make_reservation_or_null(size);
  while (!res) {
    auto status = _notification_channel->wait();
    if (status == notification_channel::wait_status::SHUTDOWN) { return nullptr; }
    if (status == notification_channel::wait_status::IDLE) { return make_reservation_upto(size); }
    res = make_reservation_or_null(size);
  }
```
`notification_channel::wait()` returns `IDLE` only when `_n_active_notifiers == 0`
(`cucascade/src/memory/notification_channel.cpp:49-60`), and a notifier lives exactly as long as a
reservation arena (`notification_channel.cpp:27-33`, arenas created with the notifier at
`reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:365-381`). So **a partial grant means no other reservation
is live on this memory space**: everything else that fills the pool is unreserved allocation.
`reserve_upto` grants `limit - total_allocated` (`reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:535-543`,
`do_reserve_upto` = `add_bounded(size, _memory_limit)`), so `limit - grant` is the bytes held
outside reservations.

**The floor.** `src/include/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_task.hpp:99-108`
```
void update_retry_reservation_floor_after_oom(std::size_t current_reservation_bytes,
                                              std::size_t live_allocated_bytes,
                                              std::optional<std::size_t> requested_bytes) noexcept
{
  auto next_floor = memory::saturating_mul(current_reservation_bytes, 2);
  next_floor = std::max(next_floor, memory::saturating_add(live_allocated_bytes, request_bytes));
  ...
```

## 2. Mechanism

### 2.1 Decision rule

A reschedule request for `oom_reschedule_exception` is **futile** iff all of:

1. `retry_count >= 1` for the task that just failed (it was created by a reschedule; a first
   attempt never fails fast, so the `+3` first-attempt partial lines per query are unaffected).
2. The gate observation recorded for this attempt says `freed_by_downgrade == 0` and
   `granted < min(retry_reservation_floor, space_max)` (the space could not grant what the
   previous OOM said the task needs, and spilling freed nothing).
3. `_tasks_executed.load() == progress_mark`, where `progress_mark` is `_tasks_executed` at the
   moment this retry was created. `_tasks_executed` is per executor and success-only
   (`gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:310`). If any task on this device completed in the meantime,
   memory may have been released and the attempt is not futile.

Conditions 2 and 3 are the reason this is safe for the contention case the 100-retry budget was
raised for (comment at `gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:339-347`, from `2ac106b2` #732): that OOM comes
from the cross-GPU clone allocation inside `lock_or_prepare_batch`
(`src/include/pipeline/batch_lock_utils.hpp:122-124` `read_accessor.clone_to<...>`; the shared
lock itself never throws OOM, `cucascade/src/data/data_batch.cpp:218-223`) while other probe tasks
on the same device keep completing, so condition 3 fails and retries continue up to 100 exactly as
today. `cuda_launch_reschedule_exception` is excluded from the rule entirely (it is not a memory
shortfall; the existing 100-retry budget applies unchanged).

Why the gate observation and not `has_disk_tier()`: `src/include/downgrade/downgrade_executor.hpp:155-161`
already documents `has_disk_tier()` as "used by callers (e.g. the GPU pipeline executor) to decide
whether an unsatisfiable reservation can ever be relieved by spilling, or whether retrying is
futile", but no caller exists (`grep -rn has_disk_tier src` -> only its definition and
`has_viable_downgrade_target()` at `downgrade_executor.cpp:401-411`). The design uses the
stronger, already-computed signal `freed == 0` (correct with or without a disk tier: 0 freed with a
disk tier means there was no convertible candidate at all) and reports the disk-tier state in the
message via `has_disk_tier()`, which finally gives that hook its intended caller.

### 2.2 Where each piece lives

**(a) `src/include/pipeline/sirius_pipeline_task_states.hpp`** next to `reservation_size_info`
(`:43-52`): a plain struct the executor fills at the gate.
```cpp
/// What the GPU executor's reservation gate saw for one attempt. Recorded on the task's local
/// state before dispatch; read by the reschedule path to decide whether another retry can succeed.
struct retry_gate_observation {
  std::size_t requested_bytes   = 0;  ///< bytes_needs after the space-max clamp
  std::size_t granted_bytes     = 0;  ///< reservation->size() actually handed to the task
  std::size_t freed_by_downgrade = 0; ///< bytes the predicate-based downgrade freed (0 if none ran)
  bool downgrade_available      = false;  ///< a downgrade executor exists for this space
  bool disk_tier_configured     = false;  ///< downgrade_executor::has_disk_tier()
  std::size_t space_max_bytes   = 0;  ///< memory_space::get_max_memory()
};
```

**(b) `src/include/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_task.hpp`** in `gpu_pipeline_task_local_state`
(after `retry_count`/`original_task_id`, `:91-94`): `std::optional<retry_gate_observation>
gate_observation;` and `std::size_t executor_progress_mark = 0;` with the same doc-comment style
("only meaningful when retry_count > 0"). No inheritance needed: the executor sets the mark on the
new local state at reschedule time and the gate fills the observation on every attempt.

**(c) `src/include/pipeline/retry_futility.hpp`** (new, header-only, no CUDA includes, same
pattern as `batch_lock_utils.hpp` + `test_batch_lock_utils.cpp`):
```cpp
namespace sirius::pipeline {
struct retry_futility_input {
  uint32_t retry_count;                           // of the task that just OOM'd
  std::size_t retry_reservation_floor;            // from its local state
  std::optional<retry_gate_observation> gate;     // from its local state
  std::size_t progress_mark;                      // _tasks_executed when the retry was created
  std::size_t tasks_executed_now;                 // _tasks_executed now
};
/// Returns std::nullopt when another retry may succeed, otherwise the reason it cannot.
std::optional<std::string> assess_retry_futility(const retry_futility_input& in, int device_id);
}
```
Rule as in 2.1; the returned string is the human-readable reason used in the error. Pure function,
so it is unit-tested without a GPU.

**(d) `src/pipeline/gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp`**, three edits:

1. Gate records the observation. Immediately before `local_state->set_reservation(...)` (`:284-286`),
   in both the downgrade branch (`:196-272`) and the no-downgrade-executor branch (`:273-283`):
   ```cpp
   local_state->gate_observation = retry_gate_observation{
     .requested_bytes = bytes_needs, .granted_bytes = reservation->size(),
     .freed_by_downgrade = freed, .downgrade_available = _downgrade_executor != nullptr,
     .disk_tier_configured = _downgrade_executor && _downgrade_executor->has_disk_tier(),
     .space_max_bytes = _memory_space->get_max_memory()};
   ```
   (`freed` is hoisted to the enclosing scope, default 0.) The `:263` WARN keeps its text.

2. Reschedule path marks progress. At `:387-389` where the new local state is built:
   ```cpp
   new_local_state->executor_progress_mark = _tasks_executed.load(std::memory_order_relaxed);
   ```

3. Reschedule path decides. Directly after the `MAX_RETRIES` block (`:349-364`), guarded by
   `dynamic_cast<oom_reschedule_exception*>(&ex)`:
   ```cpp
   if (auto reason = assess_retry_futility({...cur_local fields..., _tasks_executed.load()},
                                           _memory_space->get_device_id())) {
     SIRIUS_LOG_ERROR("GPU Pipeline Executor: task {} (original task {}) giving up after {} OOM "
                      "retries -- {}: {}", ..., *reason, ex.what());
     if (_completion_handler) {
       _completion_handler->report_error(std::make_exception_ptr(std::runtime_error(
         "GPU pipeline task gave up after " + std::to_string(cur_local->retry_count) +
         " OOM retries with no progress for original task " + std::to_string(orig_task_id) +
         ": " + ex.what() + "; " + *reason)));
     }
     return;   // same shape as the MAX_RETRIES path: no task_creator->stop(), no drain here
   }
   ```
   Everything after (`release_intermediate_data`, `create_rescheduled_task`, sleep, `schedule`)
   is unchanged. Other stuck tasks that OOM afterwards return at `:312-316` because
   `_completion_handler->has_error()` is now true, exactly as they do after the cap trips today.

**The message** (built from the observation; q05 numbers):
```

operator GPU_SCAN (index 0); [GPU:0] could grant 3,076,488,960 of the 6,637,897,728 bytes the
previous OOM established as this task's floor; 104,297,693,440 bytes (97.1% of the
107,374,182,400-byte limit) are held outside any task reservation and the downgrade executor freed
0 bytes (disk tier not configured); no task completed on this device since the retry was scheduled
```

`held = space_max - granted` is exact under the IDLE semantics of 1.: a partial grant implies no
other live reservation, so the remainder is unreserved data (parked sink output, pinned tables).
The engine does not know the word "parked"; the CN already logs `discarding every parked sender

`E/cn1/cluster.log` at 13:05:24.626) next to it, and fix 2's per-query bookkeeping is the place to
attribute those bytes to fragments.

### 2.3 Behaviour under the measured SF1000 case

q05: first OOM of task 2567 at 13:03:44.795 (retry 0, not eligible). Retry 1 (task 2593) is created
with `progress_mark = _tasks_executed` at 13:03:44.795; its gate at ~13:03:45.8 grants 3.08 GB
against a 6.64 GB floor with freed 0 -> observation recorded; it OOMs at 13:03:45.847. If the one
successful task in the window finalised in that ~1 s round, condition 3 fails once and retry 2
(13:03:46.811) is the terminal one; otherwise retry 1 is. Query error at +2.7 to +3.7 s from the
client start instead of +101.5 s. The remaining 24 stuck tasks hit `:312-316` and return; the CN
wipes the parked slots (`engine.rs:314-315`) ~100 s earlier than today, which is also why fix 2's

Per query (**inference** from the B3 offsets and measured round periods = reschedules / retry
window: q05 40 ms x 25 tasks ~1.0 s/round, q08 ~1.7 s, q09 ~2.3 s, q17 ~1.0 s, q18 ~0.5 s, q21

and q09's 56 stuck tasks make its round ~2.3 s.

### 2.4 Behaviour for the 15 passing queries

Unchanged by construction: the rule is evaluated only inside the `task_reschedule_exception`
catch, and the recorded observation only matters when `retry_count >= 1`. On cn1 and cn4 at SF1000

## 5. Risks

1. **False positive when memory would have appeared without any task completing on this device.**
   Sources considered: another query's tasks (counted, same executor), downgrade monitor freeing
   bytes (shows up as `freed > 0` or a fuller grant), CN relay/export of parked outputs (engine
   thread is one-request-at-a-time, `engine.rs:278-280`, and the stuck sender is the running
   request), cross-GPU release (frees memory on the other device). None identified; residual risk
   is bounded to memory freed by a path outside the executor, in which case the query fails at
   retry 1-2 with a precise message instead of after 100 retries.
2. **The floor over-asks.** `2 x reservation` is the existing floor policy, not this change; the
   measured chain shows the same 749 MB request OOMing at the same 3.38 GB peak on all 101
   attempts, so a smaller grant would not have helped. Multi-GPU configs with pinned tables filling
   a device could see the floor exceed what is grantable while the task might still fit; the
   progress guard is the protection, and 4.5 step 3 checks the known case.
3. **Executors without a downgrade executor** (`:273-283`, "should never happen" in production;
   the test fixture passes `nullptr`): the observation records `freed 0`, so the rule can fire
   there too. Intentional (nothing can free memory), called out in the PR description.
4. **Message text changes** for genuinely stuck queries: no code, script or test matches the old
   "exceeded maximum retry limit" text (grep of the tree; only `notes/` mentions it), and the
   100-retry message itself is kept for the cases that still reach it.
5. **Watchdog interplay**: `SIRIUS_QUERY_WATCHDOG_SECS` cannot see the storm because reschedules
   advance the fingerprint (`sirius_engine.cpp:116-127`); this fix removes the storm rather than
   changing the watchdog. No interaction.

  `fix(pipeline): fail an OOM retry chain that cannot make progress`, body states motivation
  (this campaign's 775 s), mechanism, "intentionally keeps MAX_RETRIES=100 for #732 contention",
  and the test/SF1000 notes.
- Dependencies on the other three fixes: none to land. Interactions: fix 2 (bookkeeping) sees the
  failure ~100 s earlier but the same leak; fix 3 (cardinalities) is orthogonal; fix 4b (spillable
  parked repositories) makes `freed > 0` for the six queries so this rule stays quiet while
  spilling makes progress and fires only once HOST is full and nothing else completes, which is the
  intended division of labour; fix 4a (fusion) makes the six pass on 1 CN and this fix remains the
  safety net at the next scale factor. Landing order recommended: fix 1 first (pure engine, tiny,
  makes every later SF1000 arm ~12 minutes shorter).

# SF1000 profiling: planning / cardinality / backpressure — evidence bundle and analysis plan

Build: worktree /home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf, branch perf/profile-sf1000 = d24f02c4 + 85658f09 (aggregate gate) +
9a5a4da6 (async sender dispatch) + 45dab3be (Quent probes: scan_split_read, stream hops, staging leases, CN fragment labels).
Data: /scratch/sirius/datasets/tpch_sf1000 (decimal TPC-H, one parquet dir per table). Queries: experimental/starrocks/benchmarks/tpch/queries/qNN.sql.

## Evidence (scratchpad = /tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000)
- survey/explain/qNN.costs.txt, qNN.verbose.txt   FE EXPLAIN COSTS / VERBOSE for all 22 queries (fragments, join distribution, cardinality: 1 everywhere)
- survey/plan-summary.txt                          explain_summary.py over all 22 (joins with build/probe children and broadcast tables)
- cn1/  cn4/  standalone/                           the three arms; each has runs/runs.csv (query,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start_utc), runs/qNN.rK.out(.err)
- cn1/cluster.log, cn4/cluster.log                  FE + CN logs (fragment run started/finished, declared input stream cardinality, relayed batches, transmitted batches via nixl, OOM reschedule warnings)
- cn1/dump/fragment-*.txt, plan-*.substrait         every fragment the FE sent to the 1-CN and the translator's Substrait plan
- cn1/quent/.cnN/<session>/, cn4/quent/.cnN/<session>/, standalone/quent/<session>/   Quent ndjson (task FSM, data_batch, batch_placement, memory, scan_split_read)
- standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt                   DuckDB/Sirius EXPLAIN of the same SQL (the stats-aware planner's choice)
- <arm>-cnlog.json (cnlog_extract.py), <arm>-quent.txt / .json (quent_bp.py), card-compare-<arm>.txt (card_compare.py), results.md (results_table.py)
- ../../oracle/tpch_sf1000/qNN.tsv                  DuckDB CPU oracle answers; compare-*.txt

## Tools (same dir)
explain_summary.py, cnlog_extract.py, card_compare.py, quent_bp.py, results_table.py, ../quent_summary.py (per-operator Computing sums)

## Facts established before the analysis
1. FE StatisticsCalculator.computeFileScanNode sets outputRowCount = 1 for FILES() scans ("we don't know the real schema in file, just use the default Row Count now"); every column statistic UNKNOWN. Hence every plan node has cardinality 1 and the CBO picks BROADCAST for most joins (orders 1.5B rows broadcast in q07/q09/q10..., lineitem 3.79B rows as the build side of q04's LEFT SEMI JOIN, partsupp 800M in q02).
2. Engine stream ids == FE exchange node ids; the receiver declares the exact parked row count per stream before build() ("declared input stream cardinality"), so DuckDB plans the receiver fragment with exact input cardinalities, but only after every sender finished (receiver-first rendezvous, local_exchange.rs). Nothing streams across a fragment boundary: the whole intermediate is parked on the GPU.
3. Engine OOM handling: gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp reschedules a task on OOM up to MAX_RETRIES=100 with a 50 ms sleep, then fails the query ("exceeded maximum retry limit"). It does not wait for memory to be released and cannot spill parked batches. q05 and q08 died this way on 1 CN at SF1000 (GPU_SCAN OOM, 101 s and 168 s).
4. Reserving.requested_bytes / peak_estimate vs Computing.peak_allocated_bytes (Quent task FSM) measure the engine's own memory estimation; standalone SF10 q01 requested 20.8 GB for a 5.6 GB peak.

## Analysis dimensions (workflow)
A. Planning: per query, FE fragment tree and join distribution vs the DuckDB/Sirius standalone plan; what a stats-aware FE would choose; where the translator/CN could override (e.g. swap build/probe, refuse broadcast above a row threshold, local re-planning of a broadcast join once the actual parked cardinality is known).
B. Cardinality: FE estimate vs actual rows per exchange (card_compare), engine reservation estimate vs peak (quent_bp), the receiver-first exact-cardinality mechanism and its cost.
C. Backpressure: parked bytes and dwell per fragment, staging lease held/in-transit time and max concurrency vs SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES, Reserving/Queued waits, OOM reschedule storms, nixl transmit lease_ms/write_ms, 1-CN vs 4-CN scaling per query, standalone vs CN.
Each per-query analysis is verified adversarially (two skeptics with different lenses); the synthesis ranks findings with the evidence lines and proposes changes with file paths and confidence.

## Facts added after the 1-CN sweep (13:19 UTC)
5. Supported on the CN path at SF1000 (1 CN, 100 GiB pool): q01 q02 q03 q04 q06 q07 q10 q11 q12 q13 q14 q15 q19 q20 q22 pass (15). Fail: q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 = OOM at GPU_SCAN after 100 reschedules
   (101 s, 168 s, 232 s, 104 s, 54 s, 114 s to die; 2500-5600 reschedule warnings each, see cn1-cnlog.txt); q16 = translator gap ("multi_distinct_count has a partial state this translator does not model").
6. q15 returned 0 rows in run 1 and 1 row in runs 0 and 2 on 1 CN: streams 18 and 22 (the revenue = max(revenue) join output) carried 0 rows in run 1 while every other stream was identical.
   The build has the canonical float-sum sort gated OFF (SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS unset), so the two independently computed FP64 sums can differ in the last bits. Follow-up arms cn1-canon-q15 / cn1-nocanon-q15 test this.
7. Engine executor pools default to pipeline num_threads: 4 (docs/super-sirius/configuration.md:91-94); Quent "Queued" time per fragment is the wait for one of those slots plus the memory reservation gate.
   1-CN q04: scan fragment 37 tasks, Queued sum 19.9 s vs Computing 4.7 s inside a 1.2 s wall; join fragment requested 253 GB of reservations for a 61 GB summed peak (4x over-estimate).
8. Translator comment (node_translator.rs ~1924-1931) already records that the FE reports cardinality 1 for every FILES() scan and that nothing bounds a join build side; "bounding it belongs to the executor".
9. FE plans with 4 CNs alive are in survey/explain4/ (plan-summary-4cn.txt); diff against plan-summary.txt shows whether node count changes any distribution decision.
10. Plan-node enum decode for the dumps (TPlanNodeType(N)): survey/TPlanNodeType.map.txt (4 HASH_JOIN, 6 AGGREGATION, 8 SORT, 9 EXCHANGE, 17 FILE_SCAN, 28 PROJECT, ...).
11. The engine's DuckDB optimizer runs on every fragment (sirius_ffi.cpp:135, with STATISTICS_PROPAGATION and a few rewrites disabled, :233-240); the declared stream cardinality feeds the TableFunction cardinality callback (stream_bind_catalog.hpp:44-46), so build/probe choice inside a fragment sees exact stream sizes, but FILES() scans inside the same fragment carry DuckDB's parquet estimate. The FE's fragment cut (what is broadcast/shuffled) is fixed before any of this.
12. The FE's plan DEPENDS on the number of alive CNs even with cardinality 1 everywhere: with 4 CNs most joins flip from BROADCAST to PARTITIONED (shuffle) and fragment counts rise (q02 13->16, q08 11->16, q09 9->12; q03 orders join BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q04/q12/q14/q19 BROADCAST->PARTITIONED; q15 -> BUCKET_SHUFFLE). survey/plan-summary.txt (1 CN) vs survey/plan-summary-4cn.txt (4 CNs); card-compare-cn4.txt uses the 4-CN plans (q03 exch2 = 3.23B lineitem rows shuffled, q12 exch1 = 1.5B orders rows shuffled).
13. 4-CN staging leases per query (cn4-quent.txt, attributed by time): q07.r1 747 leases / 141.5 GB moved / 92.9 s summed lease-held time inside a 1.79 s query, max 64 concurrent leases per CN; q04.r1 360 leases / 48.8 GB; q01.r1 14 leases / 0.06 GB. Session-wide per CN ~3700 leases, max 94 concurrent (arena = 16 GiB).
14. Standalone (one GPU, 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics) runs the same 15 queries; standalone/runs/qNN.explain.txt holds its plans. 1-CN vs standalone warm medians (ms): q01 5073/4882, q02 1246/571, q03 3106/3050, q07 3476/3266, q11 970/336, q15 4685/2627, q20 4171/3023, q22 943/496 (results.md).
15. Pre-digested tables added: reservation-ratio.txt (per run: tasks, summed reservation request vs summed measured peak, ratio, summed Queued and Computing seconds, wall; cn1 q11 54x, q14 15x, q03 14x, q10 6x over-reservation), cn4-transmits.txt (nixl transmits per run: count, GB, elapsed/lease/write ms, write GB/s).
16. Correctness vs the DuckDB oracle (compare-cn1.txt, compare-cn4.txt, compare-standalone.txt; rel tol 1e-6): standalone 15/15 MATCH. CN arms: q02 q04 q06 q12 q13 q14 q20 q22 MATCH; q01 q07 q19 differ by 9.6e-4 and q03 by 1.8e-3 in revenue sums (the known `1 - 0.07` FP64->DECIMAL(16,2) truncation from #1236's lowering, not a multi-CN defect); q10 differs with maxreldiff 12.3 over 48 cells of its 20 rows, most likely the same truncated revenue sums reordering the TOP-20 (verify by comparing the customer sets and the revenue column); q15 differs by 1.1e-3 on its single row and is also flaky in row count (see fact 6); q11 shows EMPTY because the query returns 0 rows at SF1000 on both engines (the bench kit does not scale q11's 0.0001 fraction by 1/SF), so it is not a defect but the compare cannot confirm it.
17. results-ratios.md: 1-CN parity T_sr1/T_standalone is 0.95-1.2 for the scan-heavy queries (q01 q03 q04 q06 q07 q12 q14 q19), 1.2-1.4 for q10 q13 q20, and 1.8-2.9 for the fragment-heavy small ones (q02 2.18, q11 2.88, q15 1.78, q22 1.90); 4-CN speed-up over 1 CN is 1.7-2.35x (efficiency 0.43-0.59) for the scan-heavy queries and 1.08-1.46x for q02 q11 q22.
18. Follow-up arms (may still be running while you work; use them only if their files exist): standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv (standalone Sirius on q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21), cn1-canon-q15/runs/runs.csv (1 CN, SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1, 6 runs of q15) vs cn1-nocanon-q15/runs/runs.csv (gate off).
19. DONE: standalone Sirius (same GPU, same 100 GiB pool, DuckDB planner with parquet statistics, pipelined execution) runs every query the CN path could not: q05 5191/2786 ms (pass, rows=5), q08 3835/3674 ms (pass, rows=2), q09 6818/5427 ms (pass, rows=175), q17 4386/3786 ms (pass, rows=1), q18 2764/2691 ms (pass, rows=100), q21 6534/6401 ms (pass, rows=100) (cold/warm; standalone-failed/runs/runs.csv, plans in standalone-failed/runs/qNN.explain.txt, Quent in standalone-failed/quent/). The CN path died on the same queries after 54-232 s of OOM reschedules. This is the central planning + backpressure contrast of the campaign.
20. DONE q15 determinism A/B on 1 CN (6 runs each): SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS=1 -> rows per run ['0', '1', '0', '0', '1', '0'] (ms ['10331', '5161', '5182', '5002', '4876', '4809']); gate off -> rows ['0', '0', '1', '0', '0', '0'] (ms ['10576', '4795', '4847', '4799', '4661', '4788']). Files: cn1-canon-q15/, cn1-nocanon-q15/ (runs, cluster.log, quent, engine-*.log).
21. CORRECTION to fact 6: the A/B in fact 20 REFUTES the simple hypothesis that the SIRIUS_CANONICAL_FLOAT_SUMS gate alone explains q15's empty runs: with the canonical sort ON, 4 of 6 runs still return 0 rows (gate off: 5 of 6). The gate only canonicalizes row order inside the update-phase aggregate; the FE plan computes the revenue CTE twice (two independent two-phase aggregations over FP64-lowered decimals) and then joins on `total_revenue = max(total_revenue)`. Batch arrival order into the merge phase (and therefore FP64 summation order) still varies run to run, so the two sums can differ in the last bits and the equality join yields nothing. Standalone Sirius keeps DECIMAL and returns the row every time. Treat this as a correctness finding about equality joins on FP64-lowered aggregates on the CN path; verify from cn1-canon-q15/ and cn1-nocanon-q15/ logs (declared cardinalities of streams 18/22 per run) and the translator's decimal->FP64 lowering (#1236, cast_to_fp64 in expr_translator.rs).
22. compare-standalone-failed.txt: standalone results for q05 q08 q09 q17 q18 q21 vs the DuckDB oracle: q05=MATCH q08=MATCH q09=MATCH q17=MATCH q18=MATCH q21=MATCH

1	# Fix 1, surgical design: fail fast at the reservation gate when a retry cannot be granted what its OOM needed
2	
3	Angle: the smallest change that fixes the measured failure with the least blast radius. One
4	engine file carries the logic, one header gains one field, one existing test file gains three
5	cases, no CN or FE change.
6	
7	Source tree read (read-only): `/home/prestouser/aocsa/sirius-stacks-wt/perf` (branch
8	`perf/profile-sf1000`). Evidence: session scratchpad `perf/sf1000/` (cn1/engine-cn0.log,
9	cn1/cluster.log, cn1/runs, cn1-quent.txt, agent-notes/skeptic-oom4/retry_stats.py,
10	agent-notes/oom-failures.md). "Measured" below means read from those files; "inference" is
11	marked.
12	
13	## 1. Decision in one paragraph
14	
15	At the reservation gate in `gpu_pipeline_executor::manager_loop`, after the downgrade attempt
16	has returned and the reservation is still partial (`gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:262-272`, the
17	"proceeding with partial reservation" branch), abort the query when all of the following hold:
18	the task is a retry (`retry_count > 0`), the downgrade freed 0 bytes, and the bytes this task
19	can still obtain (`reservation->size() + _memory_space->get_available_memory()`) are below the
20	bytes its last OOM proved it needs (`live_allocated + requested` at the failing allocation, a
21	new `size_t` recorded next to the existing retry floor). The engine already certifies the two
22	facts that make this safe: `memory_space::make_reservation` hands out a partial grant only when
23	no other reservation is alive on the space (`cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-266`
24	with `notification_channel.cpp:49-60`), and the downgrade sweep just reported that nothing it can
25	see is convertible. Nothing in flight and nothing downgradable means the grant cannot grow, so the
26	next attempt is certain to OOM again. `MAX_RETRIES=100` and the 50 ms backoff stay as they are;
27	the cross-GPU contention and CUDA-launch retry paths never satisfy the new predicate.

147	### 3.2 Fact A: a partial grant means nothing is in flight
148	
149	`cucascade/src/memory/memory_space.cpp:257-266`:
150	
151	```cpp
152	std::unique_ptr<reservation> memory_space::make_reservation(size_t size)
153	{
154	  std::unique_ptr<reservation> res = make_reservation_or_null(size);
155	  while (!res) {
156	    auto status = _notification_channel->wait();
157	    if (status == notification_channel::wait_status::SHUTDOWN) { return nullptr; }
158	    if (status == notification_channel::wait_status::IDLE) { return make_reservation_upto(size); }
159	    res = make_reservation_or_null(size);
160	  }
161	  return res;
162	}
163	```
164	
165	`cucascade/src/memory/notification_channel.cpp:49-60`:
166	
167	```cpp
168	notification_channel::wait_status notification_channel::wait()
169	{
170	  ...
171	  _cv.wait(lock, [&, self = shared_from_this()] {
172	    notified = std::exchange(_has_been_notified, false);
173	    return notified || (_n_active_notifiers == 0) || not _is_running;
174	  });
175	  return !_is_running ? wait_status::SHUTDOWN
176	         : (notified) ? wait_status::NOTIFIED
177	                      : wait_status::IDLE;
178	}
179	```
180	
181	Every reservation owns a notifier for its lifetime: `reserve`/`reserve_upto` pass the notifier
182	into the arena (`reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:365-381`), `reserved_arena` holds it as
183	`const notify_on_exit _on_exit` (`cucascade/include/cucascade/memory/memory_reservation.hpp:183-198`),
184	and `~notify_on_exit` posts on release (`notification_channel.cpp:97-101`). So `IDLE` is reached
185	only when `_n_active_notifiers == 0`: no reservation is alive on this space. A partial grant
186	(`make_reservation_upto`) is therefore issued only when no in-flight reservation could free memory
187	by finishing. The grant itself is everything the reservation limit allows:
188	`do_reserve_upto` adds `min(request, limit - total_allocated)` via `add_bounded(T& diff, ...)`
189	(`reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:535-543`, `cucascade/include/cucascade/utils/atomics.hpp:87`).
190	
191	This is also why the SF1000 storm was serialised: the manager could only get a grant when the
192	previous stuck task had released its reservation (2.3).
193	
194	### 3.3 Fact B: the downgrade reported that nothing visible is convertible
195	
196	`request_downgrade(...).get()` returns total bytes freed (`downgrade_executor.hpp:145-153`,
197	`downgrade_executor.cpp:388-397` sets the promise to `req->bytes_freed`). TIER 1 walks every
198	registered repository manager (`downgrade_executor.cpp:223-232`), TIER 2 the queued pipeline tasks
199	(`:294-300`). `freed == 0` means neither tier had a candidate that moved. In the measured case the
200	bytes are the streaming sink's parked output, which escapes the managers by design
201	(`src/exec/streaming_fragment.cpp:103-112`, finding B2); the HOST tier was configured and empty
202	(`HOST_MEM=160GiB`, `engine_settings.rs:111-116`), so `has_viable_downgrade_target()`
203	(`downgrade_executor.cpp:406-446`) would say "viable" and cannot serve as the discriminator.
204	`freed == 0` from the actual sweep is the fact to use.

233	
234	  void update_retry_reservation_floor_after_oom(std::size_t current_reservation_bytes,
235	                                                std::size_t live_allocated_bytes,
236	                                                std::optional<std::size_t> requested_bytes) noexcept
237	  {

239	    auto next_floor          = memory::saturating_mul(current_reservation_bytes, 2);
240	    next_floor = std::max(next_floor, memory::saturating_add(live_allocated_bytes, request_bytes));
241	    next_floor = std::max(next_floor, kDefaultRetryRequestBytes);

249	`live_allocated + requested` is a hard lower bound on what the same attempt must allocate on its
250	own stream to get past the allocation that failed; the resumed task re-runs the same operator on
251	the same input (for GPU_SCAN it re-reads the same split, `sirius_gpu_scan_operator.cpp:536-537`;
252	finding B3 measured the chain byte-identical over 101 attempts). The `2 x reservation` term is the
253	engine's retry sizing policy, not evidence of need, so the abort compares against
254	`live + requested` only (see 10.2 for why not the floor).
255	
256	The floor is carried across reschedules (`gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:389
257	inherit_retry_reservation_floor`) and folded into the next request
258	(`gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:855, 886`: `reservation_size = max(normal_reservation, retry_reservation_floor)`).

260	### 3.5 Putting A, B, C together
261	
262	At the gate of a retry, after the downgrade: if `freed == 0`, the grant is everything the space
263	can give with nothing in flight and nothing to spill. If that is less than `live + requested`, the
264	attempt is certain to hit the same allocation failure. Waiting cannot help: on the CN path the
265	parked bytes are released only when the receiver relays them, and the receiver runs only after
266	this fragment finishes (`engine.rs:278-280` one request at a time; `local_exchange.rs` take_ready;
267	finding B1). Pinned tables are released only by an explicit unpin. Repositories of the same query
268	are visible to the sweep (TIER 1) and would have counted as `freed > 0`.

364	## 5. Behaviour
365	
366	### 5.1 Under the measured SF1000 case (1 CN, 100 GiB pool)
367	
368	Per stuck scan task, attempt 0 proceeds exactly as today (partial grant, `retry_count == 0`),
369	OOMs, records `required = live + 748,875,880` (q05) and the floor 6.64 GB, and is rescheduled
370	(retry 1). Its retry reaches the gate after the fresh tasks queued ahead of it (FIFO). At that gate:
371	`make_reservation(6.64 GB)` blocks until the one task in flight releases, returns `IDLE`, grants
372	`upto` = 3.08-3.32 GB (measured range); the downgrade frees 0 (measured, 17,917/17,917);
373	`grantable = grant + get_available_memory() ~= grant` (CN config has
374	`reservation_limit_fraction: 1.0`, `engine_settings.rs:102`, so capacity == reservation limit and
375	nothing is allocatable beyond the grant); `required = live + 0.749 GB`.
376	
377	Does `grantable < required` hold? Accounting argument (inference, the log prints peak not live):
378	at the OOM the pool was at its limit (`global usage 107374182400`), so what was free for this
379	task equalled its own live bytes; at the retry the grant equals limit minus the persistent bytes
380	(parked output), which only grew (one more batch finalised after the first OOM in each window,
381	finding B3). The storm is serialised (2.3), so no other in-flight task's bytes inflate the grant.
382	Hence `grant <= live_then < live_then + requested = required`, with a margin of at least
383	`requested` = 0.33-1.75 GB across the six queries (retry_stats.py "requested bytes"). The abort
384	fires on the first retry that reaches the gate.
385

580	## 10. Risks

582	1. **Externally released non-reservation memory (false positive).** If bytes outside reservations
583	   are freed by something the engine cannot see between the OOM and the retry gate (an
584	   `unpin_table`, a CN dropping another query's parked slot, a concurrent standalone query's
585	   `QueryEnd` on a context with no HOST tier), the retry could have succeeded and we abort instead.
586	   Bounded: today such a task has 5-9 s of patience (100 x ~50-90 ms) and then fails with a less
587	   useful message; on the CN path fragments run one at a time per engine thread so no other
588	   query's release can arrive mid-fragment. If reviewers want hysteresis, a
589	   `kStalledRetriesBeforeFailFast = 2` (abort on the second consecutive stalled retry gate) costs
590	   one extra round (~1 s in q05) and is a two-line addition (a counter in the local state,
591	   inherited like the floor). Recommended default: 1.
592	2. **Dependence on cucascade's `IDLE` semantics.** The proof leans on `make_reservation` granting
593	   partially only when `_n_active_notifiers == 0`. Pinned by unit case 2; if cucascade changes
594	   (e.g. a timed wait), that test fails loudly before the behaviour ships.

596	   `rmm::out_of_memory`** (requested falls back to 1 MiB). Then `required` is a weaker bound and the
597	   predicate may not fire: the change is dormant, never wrong. Measured OOMs here all carry
598	   `cucascade_out_of_memory` (requested and global usage are printed).
599	4. **`break` stops the manager loop until `drain_after_error`.** Same as the four existing gate
600	   failure paths; on the CN the failing fragment's `execute()` catch drains immediately
601	   (`sirius_engine.cpp:267-278`, measured 75 ms to `fragment run failed`). A caller that bypasses
602	   that catch would leave the executor idle until the next drain; not new to this change.

2

4	and concurrency, observable, configurable where it must be, failure modes enumerated.

16	
17	## 1. Summary
18	
19	Today a GPU pipeline task that OOMs is rescheduled up to `MAX_RETRIES = 100` times with a 50 ms
20	sleep, and nothing in the loop asks whether a retry can ever succeed. At SF1000 on one CN the six
21	queries whose lineitem projection does not fit the 100 GiB pool die after 54-232 s each
22	(775 s of a 910 s sweep), emitting 17,900 reschedule warnings and 89,580 log lines, while every
23	downgrade sweep frees 0 bytes and the grantable reservation (3.08-3.32 GB) stays below the
24	task's own OOM-derived floor (4.90-6.64 GB).
25	
26	The design adds a **futility check that is decided at the reservation gate and confirmed by the
27	next OOM**, and only when four independent signals all say "nothing can change":
28	
29	1. the downgrade sweep that just ran freed 0 bytes (nothing spillable exists right now);
30	2. the reservation granted is below the task's retry floor (what the previous attempt provably
31	   needed);
32	3. no task has completed successfully anywhere on this context since this task was rescheduled;
33	4. no first-attempt task is in flight on any executor (nothing running could release memory).
34	
35	A task whose gate visit is flagged under those conditions and then OOMs again counts one
36	"futile attempt"; after `max_futile_attempts` (default 2) consecutive futile attempts the query
37	is failed with an error that names the real cause (usage vs limit, resident bytes outside live
38	reservations, grant vs floor, bytes freed, attempts). The 100-retry cap, the backoff and the
39	whole reschedule mechanism stay as they are for every other case, in particular the cross-GPU
40	batch-lock contention case that motivated `MAX_RETRIES = 100` (arrives with a full grant and a
41	first-attempt task in flight on the other GPU, so neither signal 2 nor signal 4 holds).
42	
43	Predicted effect on the measured case: each of the six failures dies ~2 s after its first OOM
44	(q05 ~3.7 s instead of 101.5 s; q18 ~11.4 s because its first OOM is at +9.3 s), the sweep
45	drops from 910 s to ~160 s, per-failure log volume from ~12,500 lines to ~400. The 15 passing
46	queries never enter the changed branch (`oom_resched=0` for all of them, cn1-cnlog.txt).

230	## 4. Design
231	
232	### 4.1 Principles
233	
234	- **Decide with evidence, confirm with the failure.** The gate knows the memory facts; the OOM
235	  that follows proves the partial reservation really was insufficient. Never abort a task that
236	  has not OOMed under flagged conditions: "proceeding with partial reservation" exists because
237	  the estimate can be pessimistic and partial grants often succeed.
238	- **Progress anywhere cancels futility.** Any successful task completion on any executor of the
239	  context, or any first-attempt task still running, means memory may yet be released; keep the
240	  old behaviour (retry up to the cap). This is what protects the contention case and any
241	  "long neighbour" case without special-casing exception types.
242	- **Keep every existing bound.** `max_retries` (100) and the backoff (50 ms) stay as the hard
243	  cap and the pacing; they just become configuration instead of constants.
244	- **The error names the cause**, with the numbers an operator needs, and reaches the client
245	  unchanged through the existing path.
246	- **One place to reason about**: all new logic lives in `gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp`, in the two
247	  blocks that already own the gate and the reschedule; the rest is plumbing.
248	
249	### 4.2 New state
250	
251	`exec/config.hpp` (mirrors `downgrade_executor_config`):

253	```cpp
254	/// Retry policy for task_reschedule_exception (OOM and transient CUDA launch failures).
255	struct oom_retry_policy {
256	  uint32_t max_retries = 100;                                  ///< hard cap per original task (today's MAX_RETRIES)
257	  std::chrono::milliseconds backoff{50};                       ///< sleep before re-queueing (today's constant)
258	  /// Consecutive attempts that (a) were flagged futile at the reservation gate and (b) then OOMed
259	  /// before the query is failed. 0 disables the fail-fast and restores the pure retry cap.
260	  uint32_t max_futile_attempts = 2;

263	struct gpu_pipeline_executor_config {

306	### 4.3 Algorithm at the reservation gate (manager thread)
307	
308	Inserted after the existing downgrade branch, i.e. once `reservation`, `freed` (0 when there
309	was no downgrade executor) and `reservation_info` are final (between `:273` and `:277`):
310	
311	```cpp
312	auto* cur_local = dynamic_cast<gpu_pipeline_task_local_state*>(gpu_task->local_state());
313	bool const retried = cur_local && cur_local->original_task_id.has_value();
314	if (retried && _policy.max_futile_attempts > 0) {
315	  auto const grant = reservation->size();
316	  auto const floor = reservation_info.retry_reservation_floor;
317	  bool const grant_below_floor = grant < floor;
318	  bool const nothing_freed     = freed == 0;
319	  bool const no_completion     = _progress->completed_epoch.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == cur_local->progress_epoch_at_reschedule;
320	  bool const nothing_running   = _progress->inflight_first_attempts.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == 0;
321	  // Second, independent trigger: the space cannot give more than everything it has.
322	  bool const whole_space_granted = space_max > 0 && grant >= space_max;
323	  cur_local->gate_flagged_futile = (grant_below_floor && nothing_freed && no_completion && nothing_running) || whole_space_granted;
324	  if (cur_local->gate_flagged_futile) {
325	    SIRIUS_LOG_DEBUG("... task {} (original {}) attempt {} flagged futile at the gate: grant {} < floor {}, downgrade freed {}, "
326	                     "usage {}/{} bytes, resident outside live reservations ~{} bytes, completions since reschedule 0, first attempts in flight 0", ...);
327	  }
328	}
329	```
330	
331	Nothing else changes at the gate: the task is still dispatched with its partial reservation.
332	Two hygiene additions on the same thread, both no-ops today for non-error runs:
333	
334	- Before `make_reservation` (`:203`): `if (_completion_handler && _completion_handler->has_error()) { /* drop task; continue */ }`.
335	  After an error, the manager must not block another ~40 ms per queued retry in
336	  `make_reservation` while `drain_after_error` waits to join it (`task_executor.cpp:97-99`).
337	- Before dispatch: if the task is a first attempt (`!retried`) increment
338	  `inflight_first_attempts`; the dispatched lambda owns an RAII guard that decrements on every
339	  exit path (success, reschedule, exception). The guard is created inside the lambda so a
340	  dispatch that never runs cannot leak a count.
341	
342	### 4.4 Algorithm in the reschedule path (worker thread)
343	
344	Replaces `:339-364` (constants -> policy) and extends the local-state copy at `:385-395`:
345	
346	```cpp
347	auto const max_retries = _policy.max_retries;
348	if (next_retry_count > max_retries) { /* unchanged: exceeded-retries error */ }
349	
350	// Futility: a gate visit flagged this attempt and it OOMed anyway; and still nobody progressed.
351	uint32_t futile_attempts = 0;
352	if (cur_local && cur_local->gate_flagged_futile &&
353	    _progress->completed_epoch.load(std::memory_order_acquire) == cur_local->progress_epoch_at_reschedule) {
354	  futile_attempts = cur_local->futile_attempts + 1;
355	}
356	if (_policy.max_futile_attempts > 0 && futile_attempts >= _policy.max_futile_attempts) {
357	  _futile_aborts.fetch_add(1);
358	  auto const message = format_futility_error(*gpu_task, *cur_local, ex, futile_attempts, next_retry_count - 1, max_retries);   // section 4.5
359	  SIRIUS_LOG_ERROR("GPU Pipeline Executor: {}", message);
360	  if (_completion_handler) { _completion_handler->report_error(std::make_exception_ptr(std::runtime_error(message))); }
361	  return;   // identical exit shape to the exceeded-retries path: report_error only, drain_after_error does the rest
362	}
363	_oom_reschedules.fetch_add(1);
364	... existing WARN at :366 ...
365	new_local_state->retry_count = next_retry_count; new_local_state->original_task_id = orig_task_id;
366	if (cur_local) { new_local_state->inherit_retry_state(*cur_local); }      // floor + pin, as today
367	new_local_state->futile_attempts              = futile_attempts;          // 0 if progress happened or the gate did not flag
368	new_local_state->progress_epoch_at_reschedule = _progress->completed_epoch.load(std::memory_order_acquire);
369	std::this_thread::sleep_for(_policy.backoff);
370	```
371	
372	Ordering argument (why the epoch is read in three places): it is snapshotted when the retry is
373	created, compared at the gate, compared again at the OOM. A completion anywhere in that window
374	resets `futile_attempts` to 0. A completion is the only event that can turn a full pool into a
375	grant, other than a downgrade (covered by `freed`) or the CN engine thread freeing parked
376	repositories (cannot happen during a run: one fragment at a time, `engine.rs:278-280`, and the
377	engine's single-flight `query_lifecycle_mutex_`, report B1).

380	
381	Built from what the executor can see; everything is a plain number, no attribution the
382	executor cannot back:
383	
384	```
385	GPU pipeline task cannot make progress and is failing the query: original task 2567 (pipeline 0,
386	OOM at operator GPU_SCAN (index 0)) OOMed on 3 attempts (2 consecutive futile) of at most 100
387	retries; memory space GPU:0 usage 107,374,182,400 / 107,374,182,400 bytes, ~94.1 GB resident
388	outside live task reservations (parked or idle batches this task cannot evict); last attempt:
389	reservation 3,318,948,864 bytes (retry floor 6,637,897,728), allocation request 748,875,880
390	bytes, peak 3,376,381,184; downgrade sweep freed 0 bytes (no spillable batches; DISK tier not
391	configured); no task completed since the previous attempt.

395	`get_max_memory()` (`memory_space.hpp:113-116`); "resident outside live reservations" =

397	allocations, `reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:525-531`; **inference**: this equals idle
398	data plus running tasks' overflow, close to but not exactly the parked bytes, so the text says

402	instance ... failed: failed to execute fragment: ..."); fix 2 (bookkeeping) is the right place to
403	append the CN's exact parked-slot totals if wanted.

439	  finalizing event carries only `success`). The aborted attempt is finalized by the task
440	  destructor exactly like the exceeded-retries path today. The per-operator Computing sums shrink

444	### 4.8 Cancellation and concurrency
445	
446	- **First error wins.** Both new exits use `report_error` (first-call-wins). Concurrent workers
447	  in the reschedule path see `has_error()` at `:314` and return without re-queueing; the manager
448	  loop's new `has_error()` check stops feeding retries. `drain_after_error` then interrupts the
449	  pool and queue and joins the manager (`task_executor.cpp:78-114`). Measured drain today: 71 ms
450	  (engine-cn0.log:61725-61735); the new check can only shorten it.
451	- **Downgrade cancellation.** `request_downgrade(...).get()` throws when the downgrade executor
452	  shuts down (`cancel_pending_requests`, `downgrade_executor.cpp:481-490`); the existing catch
453	  at `:239-244` breaks out of the loop; untouched.
454	- **Counter integrity.** `inflight_first_attempts` is incremented on the manager thread before
455	  dispatch and decremented by an RAII guard inside the lambda; exceptions, reschedules and
456	  successes all pass through the guard's destructor. `completed_epoch` is incremented where
457	  `_tasks_executed` is today (`:310`). Both are relaxed/acquire atomics on a struct owned by the
458	  `task_scheduler`, which outlives its executors (it destroys them in `~task_scheduler`).
459	- **Multi-GPU.** The struct is shared by every executor the scheduler creates
460	  (`task_scheduler.cpp:117-124`, GPU and HOST tiers), so a first attempt running on GPU 1 (the
461	  build task holding a batch in the contention case) suppresses the flag for a retry on GPU 0.
462	  HOST-tier executors' completions also count as progress; that only makes the check more
463	  conservative (delays an abort by at most one round), never less safe.
464	- **No engine-side cancel exists** (`compute_node_service.rs:449-476` is a stub; `sirius_ffi.cpp`
465	  has no abort entry). The design does not depend on one; when one lands it will use the same
466	  `report_error` and inherit the same drain.
467	- **Watchdog.** Untouched. Note for later hardening (out of scope): excluding rescheduled tasks
468	  from `query_progress_fingerprint` (`sirius_engine.cpp:113-125`) would let the 60 s CN watchdog
469	  catch storms this predicate misses.

471	### 4.9 The contention case, explicitly
472	
473	`MAX_RETRIES` was raised 10 -> 100 for SF100 Q11, `cache=table_gpu`, `num_gpus=2`: the build
474	batch is held in `processing` on one GPU while a probe task on the other GPU needs it; each
475	convert-release cycle is O(100 ms) (`gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:339-347`). That OOM comes out of
476	`prepare_for_processing` (`gpu_pipeline_task.cpp:639-665`, `sirius_physical_operator.cpp:83-115`,
477	`batch_lock_utils.hpp:67-186`). Two independent reasons the flag cannot be set there:
478	
479	1. The pool is not at its limit (the problem is a lock, not bytes), so `make_reservation` grants
480	   in full and the partial-reservation branch that computes `freed`/`grant_below_floor` is not
481	   entered. The retry floor is only ever compared with a partial grant.
482	2. Even if the pool were coincidentally full, the task that holds the batch is a first attempt in
483	   flight on the other executor -> `nothing_running == false`, and when it finishes
484	   `completed_epoch` advances -> `no_completion == false`.
485	
486	So that case keeps exactly today's budget: up to 100 retries x (50 ms + gate). The same holds
487	for `cuda_launch_reschedule_exception` (`d42ff3e4`): it is not an OOM, the gate is normally
488	satisfied, the flag is never set.

494	### 5.1 The measured SF1000 case (q05, 1 CN, 100 GiB), timeline with the default policy
495	
496	Round period is unchanged (1.007 s: 25 tasks x ~40 ms of manager time; the storm's pacing is
497	`make_reservation` blocking, section 2.1), so the prediction is in rounds:

499	| time | what happens |
500	|---|---|
501	| +1.61 .. +2.62 s | round 1: 25 first attempts OOM at usage == limit (as today). Each is rescheduled with `futile_attempts=0`, epoch snapshot E1 (E1 advanced once by the single late success, so a few early tasks snapshot E0). |
502	| +2.66 .. +3.59 s | round 2 gate visits: retried, `freed==0`, grant 3.3 GB < floor 5.8 GB, no first attempt in flight (the last one OOMed at +2.62), epoch unchanged for all tasks rescheduled after the late success -> flagged. They OOM (~40 ms later) -> `futile_attempts=1`. |
503	| +3.66 .. | round 3: first flagged task is re-flagged, OOMs -> `futile_attempts=2 >= 2` -> `report_error` at **~+3.7 s** (1 round after the earliest flagged task; ~2.1 s after the first OOM). |
504	| +3.7 .. +3.8 s | `Error executing query`, `drain_after_error` (71 ms measured today), CN `fragment run failed`, FE cancels. |

519	
520	`oom_resched=0` for every run of q01 q02 q03 q04 q06 q07 q10 q11 q12 q13 q14 q15 q19 q20 q22

636	## 9. Risks and failure modes
637	
638	| # | failure mode | when it can happen | consequence | mitigation in the design |
639	|---|---|---|---|---|
640	| 1 | False abort of a query that would have recovered | memory released by an actor the four signals cannot see | query fails ~2 s after its OOMs with a clear message instead of possibly succeeding | signals cover task completion (epoch), running tasks (in-flight), spill (`freed`); the only remaining actor is a concurrent query on another context in the same process, which the single-flight lifecycle excludes today; `max_futile_attempts` tunable, 0 disables; confirmed by an actual OOM, never by the gate alone |
641	| 2 | Fail-fast never fires | a first attempt is perpetually in flight elsewhere, or completions keep trickling | falls back to exactly today's 100-retry behaviour | acceptable by construction; the hard cap is still there |
642	| 3 | Race between gate flag and OOM | a completion lands after the gate check | the OOM would count as futile | epoch re-checked in the reschedule path; any change resets the count to 0; default N=2 absorbs one more |
643	| 4 | Counter leak in `inflight_first_attempts` | an exit path without the guard | flag suppressed forever (fail-fast disabled) or never suppressed (false aborts) | RAII guard inside the lambda; component test 1 asserts the counter is 0 after drain |
644	| 5 | Tests relying on `MAX_RETRIES = 100` timing | `test_oom_reschedule.cpp:445-560` asserts `oom_count >= 10` | none: that task's floor is 0, so the flag cannot set | keep the test; optionally speed it up with `max_retries` |
645	| 6 | Wrong attribution in the error text | "resident outside live reservations" is usage minus reservations, not parked bytes | operator misreads 94 GB as "parked" when 104 GB was parked and ~10 GB was in-flight overflow | wording "parked or idle batches this task cannot evict"; fix 2 can append the CN's exact parked totals |
646	| 7 | HOST-tier executors count as progress | HOST executors exist in `task_scheduler` | abort delayed by <= one round | acceptable; documented |
647	| 8 | Post-error manager blocked in `make_reservation` | queued retries after the first error | `drain_and_wait` join waits for a release (today 71 ms, releases are frequent) | new `has_error()` early-out before the gate blocks |
648	| 9 | Config schema change under `sirius.executor.pipeline` | existing YAML | none: old keys parse unchanged; `reject_unknown` still guards typos | parser test with a pre-change YAML |
649	| 10 | Whole-space trigger fires on a pessimistic estimate | request clamped to `space_max` on an empty space, task OOMs anyway | abort after N attempts | if the whole space was reserved and the task still OOMed, it needs more than the space; nothing in the engine can help |
650	
651	Determinism: the decision depends on timing only through "did anyone finish in between", which
652	is exactly the property that decides whether a retry can help; the outcome for a stuck task is
653	the same on every run (fail), the exact attempt count may vary by one. No wrong result can be
654	produced: the change only converts a slow failure into a fast one.
