The serialisation on the dispatch worker exists because `SIRIUS_CN_ASYNC_SENDER_DISPATCH=1` was set (capture-cn.sh:12; default off); with the default, the same drain holds the RPC open and delays the FE's next deploy stage instead (`Deployer.java:236-243, 318`). Either way it is on the critical path.
108	
109	**Corrections to the proposals.** More transport threads (b) or a non-joining dispatch worker (c) cannot deliver the claimed saving on their own: packs and fragment `Run`s share the one engine thread, so packs still serialise, and a fragment started during a drain competes with `ExportNext` in the same FIFO; the upper bound of (b)+(c) alone is the ~16% non-pack part (~45 ms per CN on q03). Packing during execution into staging leases (a, first variant) would need ~30 GB of arena per CN for q03 (15.3 GB sender-side + 14.5 GB receiver-side held 0.44-0.68 s) against 17.18 GB configured, and exhaustion is a hard failure (B6). The impact sentence "small fragments could have overlapped the lineitem scan" is wrong for the current engine (one fragment at a time, B1); only the drain itself, ~0.25-0.28 s of q03's 1.42 s span, is recoverable.
110	
111	**Proposed.** Move `export_packed` off the engine thread (needs `ParkedOutput`/`Fragment` reachable from another thread; the parked map lives on the engine thread's stack, engine.rs:262-272) and make it faster: try a larger `kPackChunkBytes` or a single `cudf::pack` for GPU-resident batches (the receiver-side copy of the same bytes is 30x faster, so the 8 MiB chunking is the suspect; inference, medium confidence). Then (b)/(c) add value. Expected gain 0.15-0.3 s per shuffle stage at 4 CNs for q03/q10/q12 (inference). Confidence high on the mechanism.
112	
113	#### B6 (confirmed). The staging arena is 87-88% full for q03 and q07 at 4 CNs, and exhaustion fails the query instead of applying backpressure
114	
115	**Measured.** cn4 q03.r1 receiver on 9102: stream 2 frames 4.8885 + 4.8423 + 4.8506 GB + 3 x 0.146 (stream 9) + 3 x 0.03 (stream 6) = 15.1 GB = 14.1 GiB of the 16 GiB arena (cn4/cluster.log `received remote batches`); Quent whole-query occupancy peak 14.95-15.10 GB of 17.18 GB per CN at +1.28 s. Frames land at +0.71..+1.01 s and are consumed at +1.30 s (dwell 0.4-0.6 s while the customer and orders x customer fragments run and the receiver waits for all four senders). q07.r1: lineitem 3 x 3.62-3.68 + orders 3 x 1.13 + customer 3 x 0.30 = ~15.2 GB per CN. q10 6.4-11.7 GiB, q12 5.4-6.0, q14 <= 3.3, q19 0.7. Lease waits are zero (cn4-transmits.txt `lease_ms` median 0, max 15 ms in q12.r1), which is consistent with a non-blocking arena, not with "no pressure". Peak lease concurrency per CN: q07.r1 63-64, q03.r1 55-56 (cn4-quent.txt per-fragment `maxconc`; session-wide max 94, WORKFLOW-PLAN fact 13) against no lease-count limit, so the arena is bounded by bytes only; per-query lease counts and GB in cn4-quent.txt are time-attributed and can bleed into the next run (tooling defect AGG-6 below), which is why per-stream bytes above come from cn4/cluster.log rather than from the lease digest.
116	
117	**Source (verified).** `src/exec/exchange_staging_arena.cpp:248` throws `exchange staging arena exhausted: requested {} bytes ... (raise SIRIUS_EXCHANGE_STAGING_BYTES)`; `nixl_transport.rs:720 rpc_request_lease(...)?` propagates the error out of the drain; `compute_node_service.rs:1302 handle_staging_lease` has no wait or retry. The arena's own destructor summary never printed because the CNs were force-exited.
118	
119	**Impact (inference, medium).** With the current FE plan the arena requirement for q03 grows as lineitem/N: ~SF1150 with `STAGING=16GiB`, or SF1000 with a 12 GiB arena, fails q03 after all the scan work is done. Broadcasting the small side (P3) would need < 1 GB of arena per CN for this family.
120	
121	**Proposed.** Short term: document `STAGING >= (N-1)/N x largest shuffled stream` in the cn-tuning guidance and fix P3. Engine: make `exchange_staging_arena::lease` block with a bounded wait on release instead of throwing, so a full arena throttles senders; or let the receiver push remote frames into pool memory on arrival (`push_packed` is already a deep copy) and release the lease immediately, keeping only the per-frame row count for `declare_input_cardinality`. Confidence high on the occupancy and the failure path.
122	
123	#### B7 (medium confidence, not adversarially verified). Per-task GPU_SCAN time rises 1.3-1.6x when four CNs scan concurrently, and at 1 CN the 4 pipeline slots bound the scan
124	
125	**Measured.** Per-task GPU_SCAN Computing (ms per ~2.2-2.3 GB task, `*-quent.json top_ops`): q03 lineitem 102 (1 CN) / 134-145 (4 CN) / 111 (standalone); q10 90 / 100-119 / 96; q12 orders 107 / 131-146 / 117; q14 151 / 240-249 / 176; q19 85 / 113-126 / 98; q07 130 / 179-186 / 142; q06 100 / 138-146. Per GB: q01 0.047 -> 0.072 s/GB, q06 0.067 -> 0.096, q13 0.322 -> 0.498. q01 additionally shows 0.5-0.87 s stalls on 10% of splits on 2-3 of the 4 CNs, varying per run, with balanced bytes per CN (agent-notes/agg-only.md section 4); the 4-CN scan fragment is 1.43x (q01) / 1.6x (q06) the ideal quarter of the 1-CN fragment, which is 26-31% of the 4-CN wall. Aggregate read rates: q01 8.2 GB/s (1 CN) vs 22.9 GB/s (4 CN); q06 20.5 vs 50.8 GB/s, so the storage has headroom over what 4 slots pull. At 1 CN all 107 (q01) / 65 (q06) scan tasks are created within 9-50 ms and the 4 slots are busy 98%+ of the fragment wall (Queued median = half the wall); the memory gate does not bind for these two.
126	
127	**Cause not identified.** The `scan_split_read` probe recorded counts only in the digest because `quent_bp.py` reads the wrong attribute keys (`bytes`/`elapsed_ns` instead of `compressed_bytes`/`output_bytes`/`materialize_ns` emitted by `src/telemetry/scan_telemetry.cpp:52-56`), and even the raw probe covers read + decode together (`materialize_ns`). Candidates: GPFS client contention on concurrent O_DIRECT streams from 16 slots, host/GPU-side effects, NUMA placement. The CN launcher cannot raise `pipeline.num_threads` because `engine_settings.rs::derive_sirius_config_yaml` emits no pipeline block (and pairs with C3: 8 slots would request 156 GB in the cold-start wave).
128	
129	**Proposed.** Split the probe into read and decode, fix the digest keys (AGG-6), then A/B `SIRIUS_CN_USE_SIRIUS_DATASOURCE=false` and buffered reads / prefetch cache with the page cache warm vs dropped; add `SIRIUS_CN_PIPELINE_THREADS` to the derived config and sweep 6 and 8 on 1 CN with Quent on.
130	
131	#### Disputed backpressure finding
132	
133	**BJ-6: "memory backpressure is absent for q03/q10/q12/q14/q19 at both 1 and 4 CN; the 6-15x over-reservation is harmless because concurrent reservations are far below the pool": refuted on the 1-CN half and on the mechanism; the conclusion (memory pressure is not this family's loss) stands.** Objection (data skeptic, agent-notes/refute-bj6): 4 concurrent tasks hold 58-80% of the 107.37 GB limit, not "far below"; the reservation gate blocked 47-178 ms per run in q10/q12/q14 at 1 CN in all three runs (see C3), 0 at 4 CNs and standalone; the engine pool's running peak reached 92-99% of the limit inside q03.r0 and q04.r0. "No arena exhaustion" is vacuous evidence because exhaustion is a hard failure, never backpressure (B6). The proposed regression guard is inverted: a tighter estimate reduces gating; guard instead that `num_threads x per-task cold-start request` stays well under the limit. Cost today is <= 0.18 s per query, so the impact ranking (planning, CN serialisation, scan contention dominate) survives.
134	
135	#### Tooling defects found on the way (AGG-6, high confidence)
136	
137	`scratchpad/perf/sf1000/quent_bp.py:98-104` attributes staging leases by a +-0.5 s time window, so the last run of each query inherits the next cold run's first leases (cn4 q06.r2 shows 55 leases / 25.6 GB although q06 moves 64 bytes per stream; cn4-quent.txt per-fragment lease counts are likewise attributed by time, e.g. q07.r1's 1-task nation fragment shows 184 leases). Use cn4-cnlog.json per-stream transmit bytes for volume. `quent_bp.py:60-70 scan_reads` uses the wrong keys (see B7). Fix both before the next capture.
138	
139	---
140	
141	## 4. What to do first
142	
143	Ordered by value per unit of work, with the expected effect and the risk. "Measured" effects are computed from this campaign's numbers; everything else is inference.

265:### PR reviewability
266-
267-PRs sometimes stall for weeks after a reviewer is assigned, simply because the PR wasn't actually
268-ready to review the moment CODEOWNERS pinged someone. Before marking a PR ready for review, please
269-do the following:
270-
271-1. **State the motivation, not just the mechanics.** Link the originating issue (`Closes #NNN` /
272-   `Refs #NNN`) if one exists; if there isn't one, the description itself should explain *why* the
273-   change is needed, not just summarize the diff.
274:2. **Scope the PR to one reviewable sitting.** If a reviewer can't get through it start-to-finish
275-   without losing context, either split it (see [Stacked PRs](#stacked-prs)) or explicitly justify
276-   in the description why it can't be split.
277-3. **Make the description self-sufficient.** A reviewer should be able to start reviewing without
278-   needing to ask what changed or why — cover what changed, why, how it was verified, and anything
279-   non-obvious (e.g. "intentionally doesn't handle X, tracked in #NNN").
280-4. **Open as a draft until 1-3 are actually true**, then convert to "Ready for review" — that's
281-   the point CODEOWNERS review requests and author auto-assignment (`auto-assign.yml`) trigger, so
282:   converting early means a reviewer gets pinged before there's anything reviewable yet.
283-
284-### Commit and title convention
285-
286-Sirius squash-merges PRs, the PR titles become the commit message on merge. Commits and PR titles follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) format for readability.
287-
288-Example of Conventional Commits:
289-```
290-<type>[optional scope]: <description>
291-
292-[optional body]
293-
294-[optional footer(s)]
295-```
296-
297-Scope is optional — use it when the change is clearly localized to a subsystem (e.g. `fix(join):`, `ci(distribution):`), omit it for cross-cutting changes.
298-
299-New contributors: put your best title — reviewers will help refine it before merge.
300-
301-### Configuration changes
302-
303-If your PR changes any Sirius configuration option:
304-1. Document the change inline where the config lives (code comments, settings files)
305-2. Summarize the change in the PR description for reviewers and the changelog

import re, csv, datetime as dt, collections, sys
root='/tmp/claude-1002/-home-prestouser-aocsa-sirius/25f3e903-c551-4a98-b7fc-a6e0ed53ade6/scratchpad/perf/sf1000'
runs=[r for r in csv.reader(open(f'{root}/cn1/runs/runs.csv')) if r and r[0]!='query']
wins={}
for q,run,phase,status,ms,rows,start in runs:
    if status!='fail' or q=='q16': continue
    s=dt.datetime.fromisoformat(start); wins[q]=(s, s+dt.timedelta(milliseconds=int(ms)))
ts_re=re.compile(r'^\[(\S+ \S+)\]')
resch=re.compile(r'reschedule \(retry (\d+)/(\d+)\) for task (\d+) \(original task (\d+)\)')
oom=re.compile(r'OOM at operator (\w+) \(id=(\d+), index (\d+)/(\d+)\), requested (\d+) bytes .* global usage (\d+) bytes .* peak allocated (\d+) bytes .* reservation (\d+) bytes .* rescheduling task (\d+)')
part=re.compile(r'after downgrade \((\d+) bytes freed\), reservation still partial \((\d+)/(\d+) bytes\) for pipeline (\d+) task (\d+)')
exc=re.compile(r'task (\d+) \(original task (\d+)\) exceeded (\d+) retries')
stats={q:dict(resch=[],oom=[],part=[],exc=[]) for q in wins}
def which(t):
    for q,(a,b) in wins.items():
        if a-dt.timedelta(seconds=1)<=t<=b+dt.timedelta(seconds=1): return q
for line in open(f'{root}/cn1/engine-cn0.log',errors='replace'):
    m=ts_re.match(line)
    if not m: continue
    t=dt.datetime.fromisoformat(m.group(1))
    q=which(t)
    if not q: 
        if 'reschedule (retry' in line or 'exceeded' in line and 'retries' in line: print('OUTSIDE WINDOW:',line[:160])
        continue
    if (r:=resch.search(line)): stats[q]['resch'].append((t,int(r.group(1)),int(r.group(3)),int(r.group(4))))
    elif (r:=oom.search(line)): stats[q]['oom'].append((t,)+tuple(r.groups()))
    elif (r:=part.search(line)): stats[q]['part'].append((t,)+tuple(int(x) for x in r.groups()))
    elif (r:=exc.search(line)): stats[q]['exc'].append((t,)+tuple(int(x) for x in r.groups()))
for q in sorted(wins):
    a,b=wins[q]; st=stats[q]
    per=collections.Counter(o for _,_,_,o in st['resch']); maxr=collections.defaultdict(int)
    for _,n,_,o in st['resch']: maxr[o]=max(maxr[o],n)
    ids=set(tid for _,_,tid,_ in st['resch'])
    ooms=st['oom']; ops=collections.Counter(o[1] for o in ooms); gus=collections.Counter(o[6] for o in ooms)
    req=[int(o[5]) for o in ooms]; peak=[int(o[7]) for o in ooms]; resv=[int(o[8]) for o in ooms]
    freed=collections.Counter(p[1] for p in st['part']); want=[p[3] for p in st['part']]; got=[p[2] for p in st['part']]
    first_oom=min(o[0] for o in ooms) if ooms else None; last_res=max(r[0] for r in st['resch']) if st['resch'] else None
    print(f"\n== {q} window {a.time()}..{b.time()} wall={(b-a).total_seconds():.1f}s")
    print(f"  reschedules={len(st['resch'])} distinct_orig={len(per)} distinct_new_task_ids={len(ids)} retries/orig: min={min(per.values())} max={max(per.values())} all==100: {all(v==100 for v in per.values())} maxretry==100 for all: {all(v==100 for v in maxr.values())}")

and only the first call takes effect.

## Reschedule Handling (OOM and CUDA launch failures)

**File:** `src/include/pipeline/oom_reschedule_exception.hpp`

Retryable execution failures are modeled as a small exception hierarchy: `task_reschedule_exception` is the base, with two subclasses —

- `oom_reschedule_exception` — a GPU operator ran out of memory. Carries `intermediate_data` (partial results computed so far) and `_resume_operator_index` (which operator to resume from).
- `cuda_launch_reschedule_exception` — a transient CUDA kernel-launch failure. `gpu_pipeline_task` translates retryable `thrust::system_error` codes (`cudaErrorLaunchOutOfResources` / `cudaErrorInvalidValue`, seen from concurrent PDL launches in `cudf::hash_partition`) into this exception rather than failing the query.

The GPU executor catches the **base** `task_reschedule_exception` and:

1. Checks if the completion handler already has an error (skip if so)
2. Increments `retry_count` (max 100 retries, `MAX_RETRIES`)
3. Logs the retry attempt
4. Marks the original task as rescheduled (skips pipeline completion tracking)
5. Transitions intermediate data from idle to `task_created` state
6. Creates a new rescheduled task via `create_rescheduled_task()` virtual factory
7. Sleeps 50ms for backoff
8. Reschedules the new task back through the manager loop

If max retries are exceeded, the error propagates and terminates the query.

## Error Handling and Draining

----
5. **Dispatch to worker thread** — on the thread pool with a CUDA stream:
   - Lock input batches and convert to GPU if needed (`lock_or_prepare_batch`)
   - `compute_task()`: iterate **all** operators in the pipeline (source through sink), calling `execute()` on each
   - `publish_output()`: call the sink's `sink()` method to push results to downstream ports
   - On OOM: catch `oom_reschedule_exception`, retry up to 10 times with 5ms backoff
   - On success: check if query is complete (RESULT_COLLECTOR sink + pipeline finished)
   - If not complete: schedule downstream consumers via `task_creator->schedule()`
   - If complete: `completion_handler->mark_completed()`
----
### `reservation_aware_resource_adaptor`

Wraps RMM device memory resource. On each allocation:
- Checks if the reservation has sufficient capacity
- If exhausted → fails gracefully, triggering `oom_reschedule_exception`
- Enables predictable memory usage per task


- `record(rec)` — on successful task completion
- `record_on_failure(estimated_bytes, peak)` — on OOM; keeps the **higher** peak for repeated failures with the same input size, so each retry reserves more

Judged from delivery: all three land as one self-contained engine PR against dev from a fork (src/ layer per the carve plan), none depend on fixes 2/3/4, and all three agree fix 1 should land first because it shortens every later SF1000 arm by ~12 minutes. The discriminators are size, signature blast radius, and whether the predicate as written is correct.

Surgical wins on every delivery axis and, after source verification, is not weaker on correctness than its own text claims. Its open question 1 (is live+requested really above the grant?) is answered by the arena accounting: check_reservation_and_handle_overflow (reservation_aware_resource_adaptor.cpp:184-214) charges nothing upstream for allocations inside the reservation, so a LIMIT_EXCEEDED OOM (:477-482) proves live+requested > reservation_at_oom, and per chain the retry grant is <= that reservation because the grant is limit minus parked bytes and parked only grew (measured: every one of the 17,917 gate passes in the six windows freed 0 and was partial; retry_stats.py rerun). So the abort fires on the first retry gate of every stuck chain, deterministically, with time-to-fail first OOM + at most one ~1 s round (q05 ~2-3 s vs 101.5 s; q18 ~9.5-10 s because its first OOM is at +9.29 s). The change is ~43 engine lines in two files that already own the logic (gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:262-272 partial-after-downgrade branch; gpu_pipeline_task.hpp:99-114 floor functions gain one field), the test file is already in CMakeLists.txt:850, no config schema, no constructor change, no CN/FE change. Half a day, one reviewer sitting (CONTRIBUTING 'PR reviewability' item 2). Its residual risk (abort without an OOM confirmation) is bounded by the hard bound above and by the cucascade IDLE fact (memory_space.cpp:257-266, notification_channel.cpp:49-60), which its unit case 2 pins.

Upstream is the runner-up and has the best test shape (GPU-free predicate table, new header), but as written its condition 2 reads the post-OOM floor and degenerates; implemented literally it could abort the #732 contention case. One-line fix, but a reviewer has to catch it. Its progress guard (_tasks_executed at gpu_pipeline_executor.cpp:310) adds one round of latency for no measured benefit on the CN path (exactly one success after the first OOM per window).

Robust is the design for a knob nobody asked for yet: config struct + YAML parser, task_scheduler and gpu_pipeline_executor constructor changes hitting sirius_context.cpp:865 and ~7 test files, an exception-class change at three throw sites, a shared progress struct, and doc changes in three files. 1.5-2 days and a near-full rebuild (exec/config.hpp fan-out 16 files, sirius_config.hpp 32). It also contains two spec inconsistencies (in-flight counter increment/decrement placement; 'HOST-tier executors' that task_scheduler.cpp:52-79 does not build). Its extra safety over surgical is marginal on this failure.

Smaller version for 80% of value: surgical already is the smaller version. Dropping the new _oom_required_bytes field and comparing the grant against the existing floor would save 8 lines but reintroduces the 2x-policy false-positive the surgical design rightly rejects; keep the field.

Acceptance restatement (all three agree, and retry_stats.py confirms q18's first OOM at +9.29 s): 'time-to-fail <= 5 s each' must become '<= 5 s after the first OOM' (surgical: <= 1.5 s after). Measurability on this box: sirius_unittest '[gpu_pipeline_executor][oom]' in seconds on GPU 0 in the fix-oom-failfast worktree; SF1000 arm A (six queries) ~3 min, arm B (fifteen, x3) ~15 min; avoid the 02:00-03:50 UTC nightly window.
